<h1 id="Makkink-(1957)-Radiation-Based-ET%E2%82%80">Makkink (1957) Radiation-Based ET₀<a class="anchor-link" href="#Makkink-(1957)-Radiation-Based-ET%E2%82%80">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Experiment 033</strong> — Python control baseline aligned with primal <code>science.et0_makkink</code> and Rust <code>validate_makkink</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Theory">Theory<a class="anchor-link" href="#Theory">¶</a></h2><p>The Makkink method estimates reference evapotranspiration ET₀ from solar radiation and air temperature only (no wind or humidity). Coefficients follow <strong>de Bruin (1987)</strong> as commonly applied in the Netherlands (KNMI) and Northern Europe.</p>
<p>$$\mathrm{ET}_0 = C_1 \frac{\Delta}{\Delta + \gamma} \frac{R_s}{\lambda} + C_2$$</p>
<p>with $C_1 = 0.61$, $C_2 = -0.12$, $R_s$ incoming solar radiation (MJ m⁻² day⁻¹), $\lambda = 2.45$ MJ kg⁻¹, $\Delta$ the slope of the saturation vapour pressure curve, and $\gamma$ the psychrometric constant (both in kPa °C⁻¹).</p>
<p><strong>Citation:</strong> Makkink GF (1957) <em>J Inst Water Eng</em> 11:277–288; de Bruin HAR (1987) <em>From Penman to Makkink</em>, TNO, The Hague.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
